title: Three Numbers from the River
locale: 山口県公立高校入試型
sentences: Our science club studied a small river because residents wanted to know whether the water was becoming healthier.
The town gave us three measurements taken at the same bridge on different days in early summer.
Each record included the time of sampling, the amount of rain before it, and a number showing how cloudy the water was.
On the first day, volunteers sampled at eight, after no rain the previous night, and recorded a cloudiness value of four.
On the second day, heavy rain had fallen, and a sample taken at eight showed a much higher value of fourteen.
The third sample was taken at two in the afternoon, after a little morning rain, and its value was eight.
Ken looked only at the three values and announced that the river had become worse and then better again.
Yui asked whether the results truly showed change, because the amount of rain was different before every measurement.
She explained that rain could carry soil from nearby fields into the river, making the water look cloudier for a time.
Our teacher agreed that this was possible, but reminded us that the measurements alone could not prove exactly what caused the cloudiness.
We also noticed that the third sample had been taken six hours later than the two morning samples.
That difference made it harder to compare the records, since the river could change between morning and afternoon after rainfall.
At the next meeting, we planned a fairer survey using the same bridge and morning time over several weeks.
We decided to write down rainfall as well and mark whether strong rain had ended shortly before sampling.
Mika suggested taking photographs of the riverbank so that we could notice new construction or changes in nearby fields.
Another student wanted to measure water temperature because changes in temperature might also affect life in the river.
We knew those extra records would not answer everything, but they could help us ask better questions when we saw an unusual result.
For our first presentation, we kept the original table but added notes about the rain and the different sampling times.
We changed our headline from 'The River Is Improving' to 'What Can Three Measurements Tell Us?' so the conclusion matched our evidence.
The town officer said our revised report was useful because it showed both the results and the limits of what we could claim.
Ken agreed and said the number fourteen was important, but it mattered just as much to understand when and why it was recorded.
I learned that good science requires patience, careful comparisons, and the courage to say what remains unknown.
fullTranslation:
私たちの理科部は、川の水がよりきれいになっているか知りたいという住民のために、小さな川を調べました。
町からは初夏の別々の日に同じ橋で行われた三回の測定結果をもらいました。
各記録には採水時刻、それ以前の雨の量、水の濁りを示す数値がありました。
一日目は前夜に雨が降らず、午前八時の採水で濁りの値は四でした。
二日目は大雨の後で、午前八時の採水では濁りの値が十四に上がりました。
三回目は朝に少し雨が降った後、午後二時に採水され、濁りの値は八でした。
ケンは三つの数値だけを見て、川が悪くなってから再びよくなったと発表しました。
ユイは測定前の雨量がそれぞれ異なるため、結果が本当に川の状態の変化を示すのか尋ねました。
ユイは、雨が近くの畑から土を川に運び、一時的に濁りが増えることもあると説明しました。
先生はその可能性を認めましたが、測定値だけで濁りの原因を断定することはできないと注意しました。
私たちは三回目の採水が最初の二回より六時間遅かったことにも気づきました。
雨の後は午前から午後の間にも川が変わる可能性があり、この時刻の差は記録の比較を難しくしました。
次の会議で私たちは、数週間、同じ橋で同じ午前の時刻に測る調査を計画しました。
私たちは雨量と、大雨が採水の少し前まで続いていたかどうかも記録することにしました。
ミカは近くの工事や畑の変化に気づけるよう、川岸の写真も撮ることを提案しました。
別の生徒は温度変化が川の生き物にも関係するかもしれないとして、水温も測るよう提案しました。
追加の記録がすべてを説明するわけではありませんが、珍しい数値が出たときによい問いを立てる助けになります。
最初の発表では元の表を残しながら、雨と採水時刻の違いについて注記を加えました。
私たちは結論を根拠に合わせるため、見出しを「川が改善している」から「三回の測定で何が分かるか」へ変更しました。
町の職員は結果と断定できる範囲の両方を示したので、修正した報告は役立つと話してくれました。
ケンも賛成し、十四という数そのものと同じくらい、いつ、どんな条件で記録されたかが大切だと述べました。
私は、よい科学には忍耐と注意深い比較、そしてまだ分からないことを認める勇気が必要だと学びました。

materials.title: River cloudiness measurements
materials.note: The cloudiness index is a comparative classroom measure, not a certified water-quality health threshold.

questions.prompt: What three kinds of information were included in each record?
questions.answer: Sampling time, rainfall, and water cloudiness.
questions.evidence: Each record included the time of sampling, the amount of rain before it, and a number showing how cloudy the water was.
questions.evidenceJp: 各記録には採水時刻、それ以前の雨の量、水の濁りを示す数値がありました。
questions.reason: 三文目に項目が列挙されている。

questions.prompt: Which sample had the highest cloudiness index?
questions.evidence: On the second day, heavy rain had fallen, and a sample taken at eight showed a much higher value of fourteen.
questions.evidenceJp: 二日目は大雨の後で、午前八時の採水では濁りの値が十四に上がりました。

questions.prompt: Why did Yui question Ken's conclusion?
questions.answer: Rainfall conditions differed before each measurement.
questions.evidence: Yui asked whether the results truly showed change, because the amount of rain was different before every measurement.
questions.evidenceJp: ユイは測定前の雨量がそれぞれ異なるため、結果が本当に川の状態の変化を示すのか尋ねました。
questions.reason: 測定前の雨量が異なるため単純に比較できないから。

questions.prompt: Choose the true statement: A Day 1 was tested at two; B Day 2 followed heavy rain; C Day 3 had no morning rain; D all samples were taken at eight.
questions.evidence: The third sample was taken at two in the afternoon, after a little morning rain, and its value was eight.
questions.evidenceJp: 三回目は朝に少し雨が降った後、午後二時に採水され、濁りの値は八でした。

questions.prompt: Why could the class not tell whether the river improved from these values alone?
questions.answer: The samples were taken under different weather and time conditions.
questions.evidence: That difference made it harder to compare the records, since the river could change between morning and afternoon after rainfall.
questions.evidenceJp: 雨の後は午前から午後の間にも川が変わる可能性があり、この時刻の差は記録の比較を難しくしました。
questions.reason: 天候と採水時刻が異なり同条件の比較ではない。

questionSetB.prompt: Where should 'Therefore, we needed more than one possible explanation.' be inserted: after sentence 3, 6, 10, or 19?
questionSetB.evidence: Our teacher agreed that this was possible, but reminded us that the measurements alone could not prove exactly what caused the cloudiness.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 先生はその可能性を認めましたが、測定値だけで濁りの原因を断定することはできないと注意しました。
questionSetB.reason: 原因を一つに断定できないという10文目を受ける接続。

questionSetB.prompt: Complete: The club planned to measure at the same bridge and the same morning _____ over several weeks.
questionSetB.evidence: At the next meeting, we planned a fairer survey using the same bridge and morning time over several weeks.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 次の会議で私たちは、数週間、同じ橋で同じ午前の時刻に測る調査を計画しました。
questionSetB.reason: 同じ時刻での比較を計画した。

questionSetB.prompt: Complete the word: Photographs would help the class notice c_______ near the riverbank.
questionSetB.evidence: Mika suggested taking photographs of the riverbank so that we could notice new construction or changes in nearby fields.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: ミカは近くの工事や畑の変化に気づけるよう、川岸の写真も撮ることを提案しました。
questionSetB.reason: new construction or changesという表現を受ける。

questionSetB.prompt: How many hours later was Day 3 sampled than Days 1 and 2?
questionSetB.evidence: We also noticed that the third sample had been taken six hours later than the two morning samples.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 私たちは三回目の採水が最初の二回より六時間遅かったことにも気づきました。

questionSetB.prompt: What is the main lesson? A One value proves a trend; B Weather never matters; C Good conclusions consider conditions and unknowns; D Later samples are always better.
questionSetB.evidence: I learned that good science requires patience, careful comparisons, and the courage to say what remains unknown.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 私は、よい科学には忍耐と注意深い比較、そしてまだ分からないことを認める勇気が必要だと学びました。
questionSetB.reason: 結末は慎重な比較と不明点を認める姿勢を示す。
